races.name: Weatherbys nhstallions.co.uk Mares' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Viscountess Nelson
runners_data.note: Class leader with Henderson/Bowen team, carries 7lb penalty but has proven hurdles form and front-running style suits Fontwell
runners_data.comment: Plumpton runner-up; something to find with the Elliott runners but open to improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Won Irish maiden point in April last year; stepped up from her hurdles debut to open her account in this sphere at Perth (2m4f, good) in April; carries a 7lb penalty but is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Elated
runners_data.note: Consistent third-place efforts suggest trip increase will unlock improvement, prominent style avoids pace battles
runners_data.spotlight: Promising efforts when finishing third in her two runs over hurdles, over 2m at Chepstow and Warwick; looks sure to be suited by this step up in trip and shouldn't be far away.

runners_data.name: My Lady d'Ex
runners_data.note: Poor bumper form leaves much to prove on hurdles debut, hold-up style risky given likely honest pace
runners_data.comment: Attracted some market support but was last of the nine finishers on debut at Newton Abbot
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten 19l and 33l in her two bumpers; steps up in trip on her hurdles debut and needs to show significant improvement.

runners_data.name: Evening Tess
runners_data.note: Improving profile with Skelton team firing, good ground suits and hold-up style could benefit from pace pressure
runners_data.spotlight: Showing steady improvement with each run, latest when runner-up on her handicap debut at Newton Abbot (2m2f, good) four weeks ago; looks sure to be suited by this step up in trip and holds claims.

runners_data.name: Frenati
runners_data.note: Must overcome first-flight fall confidence issue, but front-running bumper winner gets trip to showcase stamina
runners_data.comment: Bumper winner and she looks an interesting recruit to hurdling; needs a close look
runners_data.spotlight: Landed bumper at Stratford (2m, soft) in March; fell at the first flight on her hurdles debut at Newton Abbot (2m1f, good; 4-1) two weeks ago; steps up in trip and should run well provided that fall hasn't left a mark.

runners_data.name: Maria Mes
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with 161 days off, poor bumper efforts and unknown hurdles ability make her hard to assess
runners_data.comment: Outpaced and comfortably held at Sandown but did go off only 11-2
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in her two runs in bumpers; steps up in trip on her hurdles debut but probably best watched until she shows more.

races.paceDynamic: Viscountess Nelson and Frenati will clash from the start, both confirmed front-runners who need to dictate proceedings. Henderson's mare carries class advantage but faces immediate pressure from Frenati, who fell at the first last time but won her bumper from the front. This early battle will create a decent gallop that stretches the field over Fontwell's testing 2m3f trip. The sustained pace favours prominent racers and those with tactical speed, punishing pure hold-up horses who need everything to fall right.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Viscountess Nelson Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Viscountess Nelson settles better than Frenati in the early battle and gets first run
scenarios.body: Her class edge and proven hurdles form tells once she establishes control, with the honest pace playing to her strengths. Henderson's 7lb penalty winner has the experience to see off improving types when the tempo lifts.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Collapse Late
scenarios.trigger: If both Viscountess Nelson and Frenati go too hard early and tire in the straight
scenarios.body: The pace clash backfires as both leaders weaken, allowing the patient prominent racers to strike late up the hill. Skelton's Evening Tess and Elated benefit most from the honest gallop without being committed early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Frenati Redeems Fall
scenarios.trigger: If Frenati jumps cleanly and her front-running style proves superior to Viscountess Nelson
scenarios.body: Honeyball's mare puts her Newton Abbot fall behind her and uses the step up in trip to outlast her classier rival in a sustained battle. Her bumper win came from the front and she gets conditions to repeat the tactics.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Hold-Up Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is even stronger than expected and completely collapses the leaders
scenarios.body: My Lady d'Ex overcomes her poor bumper form to benefit from a truly-run race that suits her hold-up style on hurdles debut. The pace meltdown allows her to pick up the pieces despite inferior form.

watchPoints.text: Frenati's jumping after falling at the first flight last time - confidence could be shot if early mistake happens again
Pace battle between Viscountess Nelson and Frenati could be stronger than expected given both need to lead
My Lady d'Ex and Maria Mes both making hurdles debuts with poor bumper form - market support would be significant
Evening Tess has been improving with each run and Skelton stable in good form with 10/27 record
Viscountess Nelson carries 7lb penalty but 48-day break since Perth win should have her fresh for another front-running effort

races.name: Sun Racing The Home Of Racing Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Gore Point
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 195 days off, but his class and Racing Post Rating of 115 suggests he retains ability despite the layoff.
runners_data.comment: Two hurdle wins this summer; promising chase debut; faded latest but still has potential
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner and won two hurdles races at Newton Abbot last summer; best of three runs over fences when runner-up at Taunton (2m2f, good to firm) in November when last seen; should go close if he is ready to roll.

runners_data.name: Doctor Glide
runners_data.note: Front runner whose point-to-point wins suggest stamina, but amateur jockey's inexperience over fences could prove costly under pressure.
runners_data.comment: Ex-Irish maiden who been pulled up and tailed off in his two handicaps for this yard
runners_data.spotlight: Showed little in four runs over fences when trained in Ireland, or in three runs over hurdles for current yard; won a couple of points over 2m4f last month but this is a different ball game on his handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Atreides
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won twice in December including over course and distance, and should strip fitter after recent comeback run 19 days ago.
runners_data.comment: Dual slow-ground chase winner at around 2m4f; good effort latest; each-way player.
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent sort who was successful in first two attempts in visor, in December, including over C&D (heavy); should have benefitted from his first run for four months when sixth of nine at Worcester (2m4f, good) last month; visor returns to replace cheekpieces and won't be far away.

runners_data.name: A Little Something
runners_data.note: Finally broke her maiden over fences at Stratford and carries just 153lbs, making her competitive off her lowly official rating of 89.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up off today's mark on last two appearances; likely contender again
runners_data.spotlight: Got off the mark on her 13th start under rules, and her fourth attempt over fences, when accounting for two rivals (only one other completed) at Stratford (2m3f, good to firm) last month; runs off the same mark and this is tougher but still holds claims.

runners_data.name: Wellwillya
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won at this track in February but was disappointing when fourth over course and distance last month, raising form concerns.
runners_data.spotlight: Second of two wins over fences came at this track (2m5f, heavy) in February 2025; comfortably held when fourth of seven finishers over C&D (good) last month and needs to show improvement.

runners_data.name: Footloose Man
runners_data.note: Course specialist with four wins at Fontwell including recent course and distance success, making him dangerous despite trainer's poor 14-day record.
runners_data.comment: Dual course winner last season; a possible if recent reappearance run brought him on
runners_data.spotlight: All four wins have been at this track, the latest over C&D (good) 17 days ago; must come into the equation on track that clearly suits.

races.paceDynamic: Doctor Glide will take this race forward as the confirmed front runner, with Atreides, A Little Something and Footloose Man likely to sit in prominent positions behind him. The presence of multiple prominent runners suggests Doctor Glide won't be pressured early, allowing him to dictate a steady gallop through the middle stages. With Gore Point and Wellwillya held up at the rear, the pace will likely be moderate rather than searching. This moderate tempo over 2m3½f at Fontwell favours hold-up horses who can finish strongly, as the pace-setters may not create enough pace to set up their own chances.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Doctor Glide sets an undemanding gallop that suits the closers
scenarios.body: The moderate pace allows Gore Point and Wellwillya to be delivered with strong finishing kicks. Their patient tactics prove decisive as the early pace-setters fade in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Control
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet maintain a solid gallop throughout
scenarios.body: Atreides and A Little Something benefit from being close enough to the pace without having to make it. Their recent form and fitness advantages tell as they outbattle the front runner Doctor Glide.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Doctor Glide Wire to Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Doctor Glide gets his own way in front with no early pressure
scenarios.body: The front runner capitalizes on his uncontested lead and point-to-point wins by maintaining his advantage. His amateur rider's 7lb claim becomes crucial in a tight finish at the weights.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Footloose Man Track Specialist
scenarios.trigger: If the recent course winner can overcome his wide draw effectively
scenarios.body: Footloose Man's four wins at Fontwell including his recent course and distance success 17 days ago proves decisive. His intimate knowledge of the track's demands gives him the edge in a competitive finish.

watchPoints.text: Doctor Glide's amateur jockey could struggle if the pace quickens significantly in the home straight
Gore Point needs to be noted for market moves given his 195-day absence and morning prices
Atreides should be monitored for jumping fluency as his visor addition suggests concentration issues
Wellwillya's finishing kick will indicate whether his February course win was a true revival or false dawn
A Little Something's weight advantage of 153lbs could prove significant if the pace becomes testing

races.name: Celebrating The Life Of Trevor Schooley Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Sun Joy
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who needs the trip badly after struggling when dropped back to 2m3f last time out
runners_data.comment: Back in prime form when last seen in the autumn; contender if ready to roll after break
runners_data.spotlight: Dual winning hurdler over about 2m5f; beaten 17l at this track (2m3f) last month following a six-month break and not sure that the drop back in trip will be in his favour.

runners_data.name: Granny Hawkins
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist on a winning streak whose patient tactics should suit this uncontested pace scenario perfectly
runners_data.comment: Up in grade after her two Hereford wins but might still be improving
runners_data.spotlight: Has got her act together over hurdles and completed a three-timer at Stratford (2m, good) in April; looks the sort to continue to progress and looks the one they all have to beat despite a 6lb rise.

runners_data.name: Almuhit
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from dual-purpose campaign who handles good ground well based on his hurdles wins
runners_data.comment: Two front-running wins over 2m in four-runner Flat races last year; back up from 1m6f
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins over hurdles in February/March 2025 when trained by Gary Brown; has raced mainly on the Flat for current yard, winning twice at Newbury last summer; fourth in valuable 24-runner handicap hurdle at Punchestown (2m3f, yielding) in April; should go close if running to form.

runners_data.name: Break Point
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making stable debut for Luke Dace after disappointing at Uttoxeter on latest start
runners_data.comment: Two modest runs in low-grade AW races since leaving Olly Murphy
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success came in a Perth maiden hurdle in August last year when trained by Olly Murphy; last of ten finishers at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good) on first hurdles start for current trainer 17 days ago; needs to return to form to figure.

runners_data.name: Sixty Plus
runners_data.note: Front-running type returning after 88-day break whose stamina may not be fully effective over this shorter trip
runners_data.comment: Well beaten following an 11-week absence at Wetherby last month.
runners_data.spotlight: Completed a four-timer when scoring at Worcester (2m4f, good) last September off 1lb lower; well held in better company since, he should appreciate the drop in grade but this trip is plenty short enough.

races.paceDynamic: Sixty Plus will set the pace from the front with minimal pressure in this small field of five. Sun Joy and Almuhit will track in prominent positions, while Granny Hawkins and Break Point are likely to be held up at the rear given their patient riding styles. The relatively uncontested lead should allow Sixty Plus to dictate fractions, but the 2m1½f trip may prove insufficient for his stamina to fully tell. This pace scenario strongly favours the prominent racers and hold-up horses who can finish strongly, rather than the lone pace-setter who may find the distance too sharp.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Finishers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Sixty Plus sets sustainable fractions without serious early pressure
scenarios.body: The uncontested lead allows patient tactics to flourish as hold-up horses get the perfect setup to unleash late runs. Granny Hawkins and Break Point benefit most from this tactical scenario with their proven finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracking Works
scenarios.trigger: If Sun Joy or Almuhit successfully stalk Sixty Plus into the straight
scenarios.body: The prominent pair can monitor the pace-setter closely and strike when Sixty Plus begins to weaken on ground that suits them. Their positioning allows them to respond quickly to any move while avoiding the lone leader's fate.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Sixty Plus finds the trip sharp enough to maintain his kick to the line
scenarios.body: The pace-setter capitalizes on his fitness edge and the shorter distance prevents the hold-up horses from mounting their customary late challenges. His class advantage at the weights becomes decisive when the trip plays to his strengths.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Sixty Plus struggles with fitness after his 88-day break
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace creates a scrambling finish where positioning becomes crucial and any horse can win from anywhere. The race becomes a sprint finish where tactical positioning matters more than running style.

watchPoints.text: Sixty Plus may not handle the drop back to 2m1½f after his staying successes over longer distances
Break Point's stable debut for Luke Dace could see improved tactics after poor recent runs for previous connections
Granny Hawkins arrives in career-best form with three consecutive wins and her hold-up style suits this pace setup
Sun Joy struggled badly when tried over shorter than 2m5f recently and this trip may still be inadequate
Almuhit returns to hurdles after Flat racing campaign but his best hurdles form came over similar distances

races.name: Weatherbys Racing Bank Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Special John
runners_data.note: Prominent runner improving with each chase start, 25 days rest ideal, good ground suits perfectly
runners_data.comment: Beaten favourite on last three runs, but back on track last time out; remains of interest.
runners_data.spotlight: 3-5 over fences, his latest success at Bangor (3m, good) last month a career-best; needs to step up again in this better contest but going the right way.

runners_data.name: Ballyfinn
runners_data.note: Needs to bounce back from poor effort over shorter trip, Chad Bament's 5lb claim valuable at this level
runners_data.spotlight: Got off the mark on his fifth attempt over fences, over C&D (good) last month; nowhere near that level here (2m3f, good) eight days later but maybe he can return to form back to his winning distance.

runners_data.name: Edgewell
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who pulled up last time, needs to prove stamina reserves after spring promise at Hereford
runners_data.comment: Landed back-to-back wins at Hereford over 3m1f on good this spring.
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice at Hereford over 3m1f in the spring but has found life tougher since; pulled up at Warwick (3m1f, good) three weeks ago; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Gata Ban
runners_data.note: Quick return from Saturday's Worcester win, hold-up style suits if pace develops but needs leaders to weaken
runners_data.comment: 0-7 over fences but a close second at Fontwell latest, caught late on; leading player.
runners_data.spotlight: No match for Ballyfinn when having to settle for second place over C&D (good) last month, but opened her account over fences at Worcester (2m7f, good) on Saturday; shoulders a 7lb penalty and this looks tougher.

races.paceDynamic: Special John and Ballyfinn will likely dispute the early lead, both having prominent tendencies and coming off wins where they raced positively. With only four runners, the pace should be sustainable rather than frantic, allowing the leaders to maintain their position without excessive pressure. The hold-up horses Edgewell and Gata Ban will need to rely on the sustained gallop over this staying trip to get into contention. This race shape strongly favours the prominent runners who can secure good positions early and have the stamina to see out the extended distance.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Special John Sustains Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Special John can establish a clear advantage turning for home without being pressured early
scenarios.body: The improving seven-year-old can use his recent Bangor success as a springboard, controlling the race from the front on ground that suits. His stamina will prove decisive over this extended trip against a small field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Ballyfinn Returns to Form
scenarios.trigger: If Ballyfinn can reproduce his course and distance winning form from last month
scenarios.body: The eight-year-old bounces back from a poor effort over a shorter trip, with the return to 3m2f at Fontwell suiting perfectly. Chad Bament's claim helps offset the rating rise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Challenge Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too strong between the front pair allowing late runners to close
scenarios.body: Gata Ban can build on her recent Worcester success, using her stamina to wear down tiring leaders in the final stages. The quick return from Saturday's win shows she's in good heart.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Edgewell Spring Revival
scenarios.trigger: If Edgewell can recapture his spring form after the Warwick disappointment
scenarios.body: The dual Hereford winner finds his stamina reserves over the longer trip, with the return to a more suitable venue helping his cause. His light weight becomes an advantage in the closing stages.

watchPoints.text: Special John's jumping under pressure - any mistakes could hand initiative to Ballyfinn
Ballyfinn's stamina over this extended trip after recent disappointment over shorter distance
Gata Ban's ability to handle quick turnaround from Saturday's exertions at Worcester
Edgewell's attitude after pulling up last time - any reluctance to race would end chances immediately

races.name: Jewson Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: A Tickatickatiming
runners_data.comment: Bumper/maiden hurdle winner here in 2023; in good form and should be close up again
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success over hurdles came in a Plumpton maiden in November 2023; has shown bits of form since but was pulled up at Plumpton (2m, good) when last seen; difficult to enthuse over.

runners_data.name: Our Brother John
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with minimal recent form, 31 days since last run but hard to fancy based on poor 2023 record
runners_data.spotlight: Achieved little in three runs under rules in 2023; has been running in points since but last win in that sphere was also in 2023; hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Galactic Jack
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner down to a competitive mark, consistent recent placings suggest he's finding his form over hurdles
runners_data.comment: Best of three runs for new stable when third at Taunton last month; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Useful on the Flat in his prime; yet to win over hurdles, but has made the frame on his last three starts, since returning from a lengthy absence; down to a career-low mark and holds claims.

runners_data.name: Kates Choice
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse off the back of her first win, 4lb rise isn't harsh and recent form suggests continued improvement
runners_data.comment: 25l off the winner when second two runs back; fell early here two weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: Got off the mark under rules at the 13th attempt at Ffos Las (2m4f, good to soft) three weeks ago; 4lb rise isn't harsh and she should be competitive.

runners_data.name: Easter Icon
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course form advantage but 6lb above his winning mark, carried 5lb claim offsets rating concern
runners_data.comment: Course winner who showed signs of a revival at Stratford last month; could be dangerous
runners_data.spotlight: Has six wins on the Flat; sole success in this sphere came at this track (2m5f, good) in August 2024; still 6lb above his winning mark but was still in contention when brought down at the last flight over C&D (good) in April; holds place claims.

runners_data.name: Kylenoe Dancer
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who needed his comeback run, better effort last time suggests he's returning to form
runners_data.comment: Has some long absences in her profile and was pulled when returning from one in March
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success came over C&D in May last year; seemed to need first run back from ten-month absence and fared better when third of seven at Worcester (2m4f, good) 19 days ago; should be spot on now and holds claims.

runners_data.name: Mistress Fox
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with strong recent course form, 3lb claim and good previous effort here makes her dangerous
runners_data.comment: Better run last time out and she's bred for this longer distance
runners_data.spotlight: Is gradually getting the hang of things over hurdles, running up to her best when runner-up here (2m5f, good) last month; should not be far away.

runners_data.name: Charles Morin
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who stayed on well over shorter at Plumpton, step up in trip should suit his running style
runners_data.comment: Closely matched with Balgowan on revised terms and looks set to go well again; shortlisted
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't raced much over hurdles and shaped as though this step up in trip will suit when staying on into fourth at Plumpton (2m, good to soft) in March; beaten in low-grade contests on Flat since; place claims.

runners_data.name: Dunaden Island
runners_data.note: Sole front runner with 5lb claim, poor hurdles form but uncontested lead gives him tactical advantage
runners_data.comment: Ex-pointer; fourth at big odds on rules debut but well beaten twice since; handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: 1-9 in points; has shown little in four starts over hurdles; hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Maestrow
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with tendency to fade, handicap debut for major yard but limited form suggests outsider status
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown little so far; steps up in trip on handicap debut; major yard; worth a market check.

races.paceDynamic: Dunaden Island will lead from the outset with no obvious pace rival, setting an uncontested lead over this extended 2m3f trip. Tickatickatiming and Easter Icon may try to get prominent positions but are unlikely to challenge Dunaden Island for the early lead. The lack of genuine pace angles suggests a steady gallop that could become tactical, with the field bunching up before turning for home. This sustainable pace clearly favours hold-up horses who can finish strongly, as the front runner will face minimal early pressure but may struggle to sustain his kick against late challengers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Dunaden Island sets his expected uncontested lead and the pace becomes steady
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows hold-up horses to get into perfect striking positions, then unleash their finishing kicks when the tempo lifts. Late runners can time their challenges perfectly as the front runner begins to weaken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays Strong
scenarios.trigger: If Dunaden Island maintains his gallop and the hold-up horses fail to quicken sufficiently
scenarios.body: The leader's uncontested advantage proves decisive as he keeps finding more when challenged, while the patient tactics of others backfire in a slowly-run race. His stamina reserves outlast the late challengers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Tickatickatiming or Easter Icon successfully track the leader and kick clear before the hold-up horses respond
scenarios.body: The horses positioned just behind the leader get first run on the weakening front runner and establish a decisive advantage. Their tactical positioning proves superior to both the isolated leader and the far-back runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If the lack of natural pace creates an ultra-slow gallop that becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure test of acceleration rather than stamina, catching out both the front runner and the usual hold-up merchants. Horses with natural speed rather than tactical positioning benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Dunaden Island getting an easy lead - if he's allowed to dictate completely uncontested, he becomes far more dangerous than his form suggests
Monitor how quickly Tickatickatiming and Easter Icon get into position early - if they're slow away, the pace could become even more sedate
Check if Kates Choice and Mistress Fox are held up too far back in a slowly-run race - they need the tempo to lift to be effective
Watch for any horse trying to make an early move - in this field setup, the first to go could steal a decisive march
Observe Galactic Jack's position turning in - his consistent recent form means he needs to be in striking distance to be competitive

races.name: Cathedral Wealth Ahead Of The Field Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Jack The Savage
runners_data.note: Front-running style suits this extended trip but 78 days off and first-time partnership with Sean Bowen creates questions
runners_data.spotlight: Landed a weak handicap at Hereford (3m1f, good) in March; never threatened off 2lb higher at Southwell (3m, good) last time; Sean Bowen rides for the first time so may well have a say.

runners_data.name: Alan Bresil
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces tactical challenge over 3m2f distance with limited hurdles form to recommend him
runners_data.spotlight: Has achieved little over hurdles; second of two finishers at Huntingdon (3m1f, good to firm) 16 days ago.

runners_data.name: Fravanco
runners_data.note: Prominent racer ideally suited by course and distance having finished second over this exact track and trip
runners_data.comment: Beaten 61l on handicap debut last month; up markedly in trip for this second go
runners_data.spotlight: 0-5 over hurdles but seemed suited by the new trip when runner-up over C&D (good) in April; should not be far away.

runners_data.name: Muskerry Rock
runners_data.note: Hold-up style benefits from Harry Skelton's tactical skill but recent hunter chase win came from front-running tactics
runners_data.comment: Joined Dan Skelton for £17,000 after winning Wexford hunter chase last month; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Dual point winner who came good under rules with front-running success in Wexford hunter chase (2m7f, good to yielding; refitted cheekpieces) last month; changed hands subsequently for £17,000 and has to be over interest back over hurdles for top new yard.

runners_data.name: Good Girl Rachel
runners_data.note: Prominent style gives tactical advantage though modest overall hurdles form and lightest weight of 147lbs notable
runners_data.comment: This longer trip is probably a good move for her handicap debut; tries cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown only modest form over hurdles, including on handicap debut when fourth of eight at Ffos Las (3m, good to soft) three weeks ago in first-time cheekpieces which are replaced by visor here; hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Jack The Savage will likely lead from the front with Fravanco and Good Girl Rachel tracking in prominent positions, while Alan Bresil and Muskerry Rock settle towards the rear. The early pace should be steady rather than fierce given Jack The Savage's uncontested lead, creating a measured gallop over this stamina-sapping 3m2f trip. The race will develop into a staying test from three out, with the prominent racers having every chance to maintain their positions while the hold-up horses face the challenge of making ground late over this extended distance. This race shape clearly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can avoid a energy-sapping late charge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Jack The Savage maintains a steady tempo without early pressure
scenarios.body: The measured early gallop suits those who can race prominently and kick from two out, negating the finishing power of hold-up horses. Front-runners and prominent racers dominate the finish with superior positions throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Jack The Savage weakens significantly from three furlongs out after setting the pace
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where horses with tactical speed can capitalize on the front-runner's demise. Fravanco and Good Girl Rachel are ideally placed to inherit the lead while hold-up horses still face positional challenges.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling and the race transforms into a sprint from the final bend
scenarios.body: Hold-up horses like Muskerry Rock and Alan Bresil can unleash powerful late runs to overwhelm tiring leaders. The Skelton team's tactical expertise with Muskerry Rock becomes crucial in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Fragmentation
scenarios.trigger: If early fallers or loose horses disrupt the rhythm and create a chaotic pace pattern
scenarios.body: The race becomes tactically complex where horses adapting best to the disrupted rhythm gain decisive advantages. Good Girl Rachel's prominent style and Fravanco's course experience could prove pivotal.

watchPoints.text: Jack The Savage showing early signs of rustiness or tactical unfamiliarity with new jockey Sean Bowen
Muskerry Rock reverting to front-running tactics rather than his usual hold-up style based on recent hunter chase victory
Fravanco's jumping rhythm early on given his course experience and runner-up effort over this exact distance
Alan Bresil's positioning turning for home as his hold-up style faces serious tactical disadvantage
Good Girl Rachel's response to pressure given her lightweight burden and modest recent hurdles form
